transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because this has been going on for months, and I feel like nobody is taking it seriously. My husband’s family has been quietly interfering with our money and our reputation. Like, little billing errors will show up at work, or someone at church will suddenly act strange toward me, and people say it’s nothing when they check the records, but I know it all connects back to them somehow.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not hearing voices talking to me or anything like that when I’m alone.
Do you believe for certain that your husband’s family is deliberately trying to harm you?

Yes. I mean, I can’t show you one paper that says it plainly, but I’m certain they’re behind it. These little things keep happening with money and with how people treat me, and it’s been going on for months. People check records and say they don’t see anything, but I know it connects back to my husband’s family.
Do you ever feel that someone is putting thoughts into your mind or taking thoughts out of it?
No, I haven’t noticed anything like that. My thoughts feel like my own. I don’t feel like someone is putting them there or taking them away.
Have you been seeing things that other people cannot see?
No, I haven’t been seeing things that other people can’t see. Nothing like that, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or doesn’t make sense?
No, not really. I mean, people may not agree with what I’m saying, but I don’t think they’ve said I’m hard to follow or that I’m not making sense.
Have you found yourself losing interest in things you used to care about?

No, I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest. I still get up and go to work, do my billing clerk duties, keep the house going. I still like gardening and painting when I have time. The main problem is more when I try to warn people about what my in-laws are doing—then things get difficult.
Do you ever feel that ordinary events or comments from other people are actually directed specifically at you?

Yes… I do feel that sometimes. Like if there’s a little billing error at work, or someone at church suddenly acts strange toward me, I don’t think it’s just random. It feels connected to what my husband’s family has been doing—quietly messing with our money and our reputation. Even when people pull up records and say it doesn’t show anything, I know it ties back to them somehow.
Did these beliefs about your husband’s family begin very suddenly, over a few days?
No, not over just a few days. It’s been going on for about nine months now, since the trouble started with my husband’s family over money and the holiday expectations. It kind of built from there.
Do you believe your husband’s family has abilities or methods that ordinary people could not realistically have, such as secretly controlling events in impossible ways?

I don’t mean like magic or anything impossible. I just know they have ways of doing things quietly, through people or paperwork, and it keeps showing up around me—like small billing errors at work, or people at church acting different toward me. Even when someone says the records don’t show anything, I still believe it ties back to them messing with our money and our name.
Before this started with your husband’s family, did you generally tend to distrust other people’s motives?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I wouldn’t have called myself a suspicious person before all this. I’d notice things sometimes, like anybody does, but I don’t think I went around assuming people had bad motives.
Do you ever feel that outside forces are controlling your actions or movements?
No, I don’t feel like something outside me is moving my body or making me do things. My actions feel like my own.
Since this began, have you had trouble keeping up with your work or daily responsibilities?

Mostly I keep up with things. I still get up and go to work, do my billing clerk duties, take care of the house, and I still garden or paint when I can.

The trouble is more when I try to explain or warn people about what my in-laws are doing. That’s when it can interfere, because people don’t want to hear it or they act like I’m making it a problem.
Have you heard voices speaking to you when no one else was there?
No, I haven’t had voices talking to me when no one’s there. I might think things over in my own head, but I don’t hear someone speaking to me.
Have you noticed your emotions feeling unusually flat or less expressive than they used to?
I don’t think so. I mean, I still feel upset or happy or worried like usual, and people can usually tell how I’m feeling. I haven’t noticed myself being flat or anything like that.
If clear proof showed that your husband’s family was not involved, would you be able to accept that?

I don’t think so, because the proof people keep talking about never explains the whole thing. They can pull up records or say it was just a billing error, or that someone at church was just acting odd, but I know how it all connects back to his family. They’re quiet about it, but they’ve been messing with our money and our name for months.
During this time, have you had a period of feeling unusually depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I don’t think I’ve been depressed most of the day nearly every day. I’ve been stressed and upset at times, sure, but not like constantly depressed every day.
Do you ever feel that other people can hear or know your thoughts as if your mind were somehow open to them?
No, I don’t think people can hear my thoughts or anything like that. I’ve never felt like my mind was open to other people.
Aside from your concerns about your husband’s family, have you ever had a period of at least a month when you heard voices or had other experiences that other people said were not real?
No, not really. I haven’t had a month where I was hearing voices or seeing things other people said weren’t there. It’s more about what’s been happening with his family, not anything like voices.
Before these problems with your husband’s family began, did your distrust of other people ever cause serious problems in your close relationships?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve always been a little cautious with people, but before all this with his family, I don’t think it caused serious problems in my close relationships.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent, non-bizarre persecutory delusional belief lasting about nine months that her husband's family is covertly interfering with finances and reputation, with strong conviction despite contrary evidence. Schizophrenia is less likely because she denies hallucinations, thought insertion/withdrawal, passivity, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, and marked functional decline. Paranoid personality disorder is less likely because she did not describe a longstanding pervasive suspiciousness predating this episode; instead, the beliefs emerged after a conflict and became fixed and delusional.
